question: How many three-digit whole numbers have at least one 7 or at least one 9 as digits?
solution:
Count the complement: three-digit numbers with neither 7 nor 9. The hundreds digit has 7 choices (1 through 8 except 7). The tens and units digits each have 8 choices (0 through 9 except 7 and 9). Thus 7 · 8 · 8 = 448 numbers have neither digit. There are 999 − 100 + 1 = 900 three-digit numbers, so 900 − 448 = 452 have at least one 7 or 9.
Final answer: 452
